strengths: Novel and well-motivated core insight that self-attention maps in diffusion models encode instance-level structure, with clear intuition for why this occurs during semantic-to-instance denoising transitions
Comprehensive experimental validation across 7+ benchmarks with proper ablation studies (Table 3) demonstrating each component's contribution in both unsupervised and weakly-supervised settings

Strong technical execution with well-designed components: principled IEP identification via KL divergence, ABDiv metric for edge extraction without manual tuning, one-step distillation with efficiency (8% overhead)
Excellent reproducibility with detailed supplementary algorithms, promised code release, explicit hyperparameters, and clear implementation guidance enabling independent reproduction
Consistent and practically meaningful improvements (+4.4 AP on COCO without instance labels; +1.7 PQ for weakly-supervised) with demonstrated utility for seeding SAM and open-vocabulary detectors
Clear presentation with effective visual explanations (Figs. 1, 4, 6, 8) and comprehensive qualitative results (Figures 13-18) showing method generalization across diverse scenarios
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual technical components: KL divergence for timestep selection is straightforward, ABDiv is a simple divergence measure, one-step distillation is standard practice, and BGP adapts existing random walk methods with minimal innovation

Insufficient theoretical understanding of why self-attention encodes instance boundaries, why KL divergence is optimal (Table 4 shows alternatives like JSD/MSE/MAE are competitively close), and which architectural properties enable this behavior

Strong dependence on specific diffusion model (SD 3.5-L) with no systematic evaluation on other popular diffusion models (DALL-E 3, Midjourney, etc.) and fixed hyperparameters (IEP=100 steps, τ_BGP=0.5) without sensitivity analysis or per-model tuning guidance

Computational cost underrepresented: '8% overhead' is relative to baseline only; Table 6 shows substantial training VRAM (2-20GB); inference requires multiple forward passes but total wall-clock time not compared with baselines; practical deployment significantly more expensive than traditional methods

Limited edge detector comparison relying on qualitative results (Fig. 10) without quantitative metrics (BSDS-500, F-measures); missing comparison with recent neural edge detectors; claim of outperforming edge detectors lacks strong evidence

Moderate empirical improvements (+4.4 AP on COCO is meaningful but not dramatic; +1.7 PQ over point-supervised methods; substantial performance gaps versus fully-supervised methods remain) and lack of cross-dataset generalization studies (train/test on different distributions)

Empirical method design choices lacking principled justification: 4-neighborhood ABDiv selection not explained; reconstruction loss threshold not analyzed; BGP convergence criterion (IoU > 0.5) without rigorous justification; IEP design alternatives not explored

Presentation complexity with method insights scattered across Sections 3.2-3.5, heavy appendix reliance for complete understanding, dense Figure 4, and notational inconsistencies; missing failure case analysis and small-object performance discussion

Baseline comparison fairness concerns: TRACE uses diffusion backbone while ProMerge uses CNN (not comparable); different pretraining data across methods; SAM's native instance segmentation capabilities not fully explored in comparisons

Reproducibility gaps at review time (code not available) and missing implementation details (per-model timestep adaptation strategy, reconstruction loss threshold sensitivity, training stability analysis)

strengths: Novel and creative insight that diffusion model self-attention encodes instance-level structure for annotation-free instance edge detection
Comprehensive experimental validation across 7 diverse benchmarks (COCO, VOC, LVIS, KITTI, Objects365, SA-1B) with strong and consistent improvements over baselines

Well-motivated technical approach with principled components: KL divergence-based IEP identification supported by information-theoretic grounding (Appendix D), ABDiv for boundary extraction, and efficient one-step edge decoder
Practical impact and broad applicability: annotation-free training, integrates with existing diffusion models, enables downstream tasks (panoptic segmentation, SAM, open-vocabulary detection)
Thorough experimental analysis including detailed ablation studies (Tables 3, 5, 9-11) demonstrating component contributions and design choice justifications
Clear methodological presentation with comprehensive algorithm descriptions and reproducibility details
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: individual components (self-attention analysis, KL divergence, edge detection + propagation) are established techniques; primary contribution is their engineering combination rather than fundamental innovation

Theoretical justification incomplete: while Appendix D provides information-theoretic perspective, the paper assumes self-attention peaks at instance boundaries empirically without deeply explaining the underlying mechanism; connection between Fisher information and boundary emergence needs stronger development

Concerning generalization issues on out-of-distribution domains: satellite imagery shows large performance drop (65.4→50.3 AP^inst on HRSID), medical imaging degrades significantly (Table 15), with limited analysis and no clear adaptation strategy provided

Edge quality evaluation incomplete: Table 6 uses limited edge detector comparisons; thorough comparison with recent methods (RCF, DexiNed) mentioned in related work is missing; edge metrics feel secondary to main segmentation focus

Method limitations under-explored: fixed 100-step IEP across images may be suboptimal with no per-image adaptation analysis; uncertainty masking scheme (μ ± σ) is ad-hoc; critical BGP refinement step receives minimal ablation; no systematic analysis of diffusion model backbone choice effects

Computational cost analysis incomplete: Table 7 reports costs only for generating pseudo-labels, not total training pipeline; missing comparison of total cost vs. manual annotation or semi-supervised alternatives

Presentation and clarity concerns: dense notation with many acronyms (IEP, ABDiv, BGP, SAM) impacts readability; some notation inconsistencies; connection between early diffusion timesteps and final predictions could be more intuitive

Limited ablation on diffusion model dependence: no systematic study of how different model choices, capacities, or text prompts affect results; unclear generalization to smaller models or different architectures

strengths: Novel insight that diffusion model self-attention encodes instance-level boundary information, well-demonstrated through ablations
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 11 real-world benchmarks (COCO, VOC, LVIS, KITTI, Objects365, SA-1B) with consistent improvements
Strong empirical results: +4.4 AP on COCO with only 6% overhead, +1.7 FQ on weakly-supervised panoptic without instance annotations
Thorough ablation studies clearly demonstrating the contribution of each component (IEP, ABDiv, Distill, BGP)
Practical efficiency with ~2% inference latency overhead and 0.1MB edge decoder
Clear presentation with intuitive figures and well-organized narrative
Honest treatment of limitations including failure cases on satellite and medical imagery
Detailed algorithms, hyperparameters, and implementation details supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty—primarily combines existing techniques (attention analysis, edge detection, self-distillation, mask refinement) rather than introducing fundamentally new methods
Shallow theoretical understanding of why diffusion models encode instance structure; information-theoretic analysis in Appendix D feels post-hoc rather than providing deep insights
Complete failure on medical imaging and poor performance on satellite imagery with tiny objects suggests over-reliance on natural image priors and limits practical applicability
Insufficient analysis of hyperparameter sensitivity (e.g., IEP step size, ABDiv thresholding with μ±σ scheme, 100-step inversion choices)
Baseline comparisons incomplete—missing recent unsupervised instance segmentation methods and foundation models (e.g., SAM variants)
Weakly-supervised panoptic setting is non-standard (tag-supervised), and open-vocabulary application (Table 13) feels tangential to the core contribution
Uncertainty masking scheme in Algorithm 2 lacks principled justification beyond empirical thresholding
Limited analysis of generalization across diffusion model architectures; method dependence on pretrained models reduces broader applicability
